points.description: States a correct difference between asynchronous and synchronous transmission. Asynchronous: each character is sent as an individual self-contained unit framed by a start bit and stop bit (simple/cheap, lower transmission rate). Synchronous: many characters are grouped into a continuous stream/frame, delimited by SYN/flag, needing sender-receiver synchronization (more complex, higher rate). Both modes must be contrasted (at least the key distinction: per-character start/stop bits vs. blocks/frames of characters).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only one mode is correctly described, or the contrast is vague (e.g. only 'synchronous is faster').

levels.says: Describes only one mode correctly (or gives a correct but one-sided description without contrasting with the other).

rubric.notes: Full mark for correctly contrasting asynchronous (character-by-character with start/stop bits, slower, simpler) and synchronous (blocks/frames of characters, flag/SYN delimiters, synchronization, faster). Half mark if only one mode is correctly described or the contrast is vague. No mark for wrong or swapped descriptions.
